title: P02 follow-up: NorMuon per-neuron second-moment row normalization on top of Polar Express Muon
description: P02 follow-up: after each Muon orthogonalization, divide every output neuron's row of the update by the running (beta2 0.95) RMS of that neuron's orthogonalized updates and restore the matrix's Frobenius norm (NorMuon, Li et al. 2025), keeping Polar Express, split-QKV, RMS shape scale, LR, momentum, 10x decay and everything else of 081-claude unchanged. Equalizing per-neuron step sizes mostly changes the tall fc1 matrices, where orthogonalized rows get uneven leverage-score norms, so hidden MLP neurons train more uniformly and the RL stage should start from a model with fewer under-trained features and better round-1 target coverage.
hypothesis: The orthogonalized update of a tall (1024,256) fc1 matrix has row norms equal to the leverage scores of its gradient, so some hidden neurons get persistently large steps and others persistently small ones, independent of how useful they are; with ~4700 steps in 300 s the small-step neurons stay near their orthogonal init. NorMuon's per-neuron adaptive normalization equalizes the per-neuron update RMS over time at unchanged total step size, which the NorMuon paper reports as an 11-22% training-efficiency gain over Muon at 124M-1.5B scale; at our scale that should translate into a slightly better-trained, equally plastic starting point for expert iteration. Square/wide matrices are nearly unaffected, so any effect comes almost entirely from fc1.
expected_delta: -40 to +30 theorems at >=7 against 081-claude's 404 (central guess -5: 081's +48 over 078 was partly seed luck, so regression to the mean makes a keep hard even if NorMuon helps slightly); pretraining steps within -3% to +0% of 081's 4682/4732/4769 (extra elementwise work only); final val loss equal or up to 0.003 lower than 081's 0.0950/0.0912/0.0964; held-out greedy within +-0.005 of 081; RL sampling speed within +-10% of 081

arch.change: none versus 081-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV NorMuon (Polar Express orthogonalization, per-neuron second-moment row normalization, Frobenius norm restored, RMS-matched shape scale) on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 081-claude except the NorMuon row normalization)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: unchanged from 078/081-claude: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix, applied after the NorMuon step, so every Muon update keeps element RMS ~1/16 times lr
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: unchanged from 081-claude: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients, five bf16 iterations
muon.normalization: unchanged from 081-claude: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) before the Polar Express iterations
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

normuon.change: CHANGED (new): after orthogonalization and un-transposing, in fp32: v <- lerp(v, mean over input columns of update^2, 1 - 0.95) per output row (neuron); update <- update / (sqrt(v) + 1e-10); update <- update * (Frobenius norm before this step) / (Frobenius norm after + 1e-10). The Frobenius-norm restore follows the NorMuon reference implementation (zichongli5/NorMuon normuon_update), so each matrix's step size is unchanged and only its split across neurons moves; then the existing RMS shape scale and lr-coupled decoupled decay apply.
normuon.state: one fp32 (rows,1) buffer per Muon matrix, zero-initialized; for qkv.weight (768,256) it is viewed as (3,256,1) so Q, K and V rows each get their own running RMS and each Q/K/V slab restores its own Frobenius norm. No bias correction (a uniform per-matrix factor that the Frobenius restore cancels).
normuon.where_it_bites: Tall fc1 (1024,256): orthogonalized rows have leverage-score norms (mean squared row norm 1/4, uneven across hidden neurons), which NorMuon equalizes over time. Square Q/K/V/proj and wide fc2 (256,1024) and head (99,256; vocab 99) have near-orthonormal rows already, so only the Polar Express slack (singular values ~0.86-1.14) and step-to-step fluctuations are corrected there.
normuon.source: Li, Liu, Liang, Chen, Zhao, 'NorMuon: Making Muon more efficient and scalable' (2025, arXiv 2510.05491); reference code github.com/zichongli5/NorMuon
normuon.local_check: CPU: GPT(99,5,256,8) builds 4,000,000 params; three muon_step calls on random grads keep all 21 matrices finite with per-element step RMS equal across qkv/proj/fc1/fc2 (4.7-4.9e-4 per step averaged over three momentum steps at lr 0.01); buffers (768,1) qkv, (256,1) proj/fc2, (1024,1) fc1, (99,1) head.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states (momentum and NorMuon second moments) are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 081-claude: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 081-claude.
